# Carrying the same session on through quit and into a replay. The
# panels are wired to a flag that says a game is set up; getting that
# wrong showed the next player the last player's quadrant, or an empty

tm send-keys -t "$pane" 'quit' Enter
if ! wait_for 'score recorded'; then
	fail "replay: quit did not reach the end-of-game questions"

unwanted() {
	if screen | grep -qF "$2"; then fail "$1"; dump; fi
}

# Wait for $2 to leave the screen. A prompt is printed before the
# panels beside it are redrawn, so asking the instant the text appears
# can catch the previous game still framed for a few milliseconds --
# a race that would report a bug nobody has. Something that is meant to
# be gone goes within the timeout; something that is not, never does.
wait_gone() {
	i=0
	while [ "$i" -lt 40 ]; do
		screen | grep -qF "$2" || return 0
		i=$((i + 1))
		sleep 0.1
	done
	fail "$1"
	dump
}

1	#!/bin/sh
2	# Drives the full-screen display through a real terminal.
3	#
4	# Everything else in the suite talks to the game through pipes, which
5	# reaches the no-terminal fallback but never exercises curses itself.
6	# This one runs the game inside tmux so there is a genuine pty, and
7	# reads the screen back the way a player would see it.
8	#
9	# It covers the ways into a running game -- answering the setup
10	# questions, giving the answers on the command line, thawing a saved
11	# game, and starting a second game after quitting -- because each of
12	# them arrives at the panels differently. It also covers the two
13	# refusals only a real terminal can produce: one curses cannot drive,
14	# and one too small for the panels. Both have to fall back to the
15	# classic display and keep playing.
16	#
17	# The size matters. 80x24 is what most terminal emulators open at and
18	# 72x24 is the smallest the TUI accepts; at both the message window is
19	# only ten lines, so the startup banner overflows it -- which is how
20	# the pager came to be waiting for a keystroke before the game had
21	# asked the player anything, and to eat the first letter of the answer.
22	#
23	# Usage: tui.sh /path/to/sst
24	# Exits 77 (ctest SKIP_RETURN_CODE) when there is no tmux to run in.
25	#
26	# Needs a sleep that takes a fraction, which GNU and BSD both have but
27	# POSIX does not promise; busybox would need whole seconds.
28	
29	set -u
30	
31	SST="${1:-./sst}"
32	case "$SST" in
33		/*) ;;
34		*) SST="$(pwd)/$SST" ;;
35	esac
36	srcdir=$(unset CDPATH; cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd)
37	
38	if ! command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1; then
39		# A developer without tmux gets a skip. CI does not: this is the
40		# only test that runs curses at all, and a green build that quietly
41		# skipped it would be worse than no test.
42		if [ -n "${CI:-}" ]; then
43			echo "FAIL: tmux is missing on CI, so the TUI went untested" >&2
44			exit 1
45		fi
46		echo "SKIP: tmux is not installed, so there is no pty to test in" >&2
47		exit 77
48	fi
49	if [ ! -x "$SST" ]; then
50		echo "FAIL: $SST is not executable" >&2
51		exit 1
52	fi
53	
54	# Run on a socket of our own, never the default one. A developer's tmux
55	# server is usually sitting on the default socket with a day's real work
56	# in it, and anything server-wide -- this script's cleanup, or an agent
57	# tidying up after driving the TUI by hand -- takes that down too. -L
58	# buys a private server, so cleanup can be as blunt as it needs to be.
59	socket="sst-tui-$$"
60	session="tui"
61	pane="$session:0.0"
62	
63	# -f /dev/null as well as -L: a private socket is not a private config,
64	# and `set -g base-index 1` -- one of the commoner things people put in
65	# ~/.tmux.conf -- moves the pane out from under the name used below, so
66	# every capture comes back empty and the game gets blamed for it.
67	tm() { tmux -f /dev/null -L "$socket" "$@"; }
68	
69	# tmux leaves the socket file behind when the server exits, so a suite
70	# that ran often would slowly fill the directory with dead ones. This is
71	# where tmux puts them on both Linux and macOS: $TMUX_TMPDIR if it is
72	# set, /tmp otherwise.
73	cleanup() {
74		tm kill-server 2>/dev/null
75		rm -f "${TMUX_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/tmux-$(id -u)/$socket"
76	}
77	
78	# The saved-game cases write a .trk file, which the game puts in the
79	# directory it is playing in. That must not be the source tree.
80	work=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/sst-tui.XXXXXX")
81	if [ -z "${work:-}" ] || [ ! -d "$work" ]; then
82		echo "FAIL: could not create a temporary directory" >&2
83		exit 1
84	fi
85	
86	finish() { cleanup; rm -rf "$work"; }
87	trap 'finish' EXIT
88	trap 'finish; exit 130' INT
89	trap 'finish; exit 143' TERM
90	trap 'finish; exit 129' HUP
91	
92	fails=0
93	fail() {
94		printf 'FAIL: %s\n' "$1" >&2
95		fails=$((fails + 1))
96	}
97	
98	screen() { tm capture-pane -t "$pane" -p 2>/dev/null; }
99	
100	dump() {
101		printf '  --- screen ---\n' >&2
102		screen | sed 's/^/  | /' >&2
103	}
104	
105	# Wait until the screen shows $1, up to about eight seconds. Polling
106	# beats a fixed sleep: curses paints in its own time, and a machine
107	# under load should not turn into a failure.
108	wait_for() {
109		i=0
110		while [ "$i" -lt 80 ]; do
111			if screen | grep -qF "$1"; then return 0; fi
112			i=$((i + 1))
113			sleep 0.1
114		done
115		return 1
116	}
117	
118	# Answer any paging prompts until the command prompt comes back. A
119	# space is only ever sent while a pause is actually showing, so this
120	# cannot quietly paper over a pause that should not have been there.
121	to_command() {
122		i=0
123		while [ "$i" -lt 40 ]; do
124			screen | grep -qF 'COMMAND' && return 0
125			if screen | grep -qE 'CONTINUE|HIT SPACE BAR'; then
126				tm send-keys -t "$pane" Space
127			fi
128			i=$((i + 1))
129			sleep 0.25
130		done
131		return 1
132	}
133	
134	want() {
135		screen | grep -qF "$2" || { fail "$1"; dump; }
136	}
137	
138	want_re() {
139		screen | grep -qE "$2" || { fail "$1"; dump; }
140	}
141	
142	# The quadrant panel's title carries coordinates only while a game is
143	# set up; without one the box keeps its bare " Quadrant " label, so a
144	# fixed-string match for that would pass on the empty frame it is
145	# supposed to catch.
146	QUADTITLE=' Quadrant [0-9]+ - [0-9]+ '
147	
148	unwanted() {
149		if screen | grep -qF "$2"; then fail "$1"; dump; fi
150	}
151	
152	# Wait for $2 to leave the screen. A prompt is printed before the
153	# panels beside it are redrawn, so asking the instant the text appears
154	# can catch the previous game still framed for a few milliseconds --
155	# a race that would report a bug nobody has. Something that is meant to
156	# be gone goes within the timeout; something that is not, never does.
157	wait_gone() {
158		i=0
159		while [ "$i" -lt 40 ]; do
160			screen | grep -qF "$2" || return 0
161			i=$((i + 1))
162			sleep 0.1
163		done
164		fail "$1"
165		dump
166	}
167	
168	# tmux takes a shell command line, not an argument list, so the path
169	# has to survive being quoted into one.
170	sstq=$(printf "%s" "$SST" | sed "s/'/'\\\\''/g")
171	
172	# Start the game on a terminal $1 wide by $2 tall, passing $3 (if any)
173	# on the command line and running it under $4 (if any, an `env ...`
174	# prefix). It reads sst.doc from the current directory, and dies with
175	# the session.
176	startdir="$srcdir"	# where the game plays; sst.doc has to be here
177	start() {
178		cleanup
179		tm new-session -d -x "$1" -y "$2" -s "$session" -c "$startdir" \
180			"${4:-} '$sstq' -t ${3:-}; sleep 30" 2>/dev/null || {
181			echo "FAIL: could not start a ${1}x${2} tmux session" >&2
182			exit 1
183		}
184	}
185	
186	# --- the game asks before it pauses, at every size it accepts -------
187	# 80x24 is what most emulators open at; 72x24 is the smallest the TUI
188	# will run in. The banner is longer than the message window at both, so
189	# it scrolls -- ordinary. Stopping to ask for a keystroke is not:
190	# nothing has been asked yet, so there is no reader to wait for, and
191	# the prompt sits exactly where the player is about to type an answer.
192	for size in 80x24 72x24; do
193		cols=${size%x*}
194		rows=${size#*x}
195		start "$cols" "$rows"
196	
197		if ! wait_for 'regular, tournament, or frozen'; then
198			fail "$size: the game never asked its first question"
199			dump
200			exit 1
201		fi
202		# Curses is really running, not the classic display falling back
203		# inside the pty. Without this every assertion below is satisfied
204		# by the plain path, and a broken tui_init() would still look
205		# green -- from a script whose whole point is to exercise curses.
206		# The panel titles are drawn in TUI mode and nowhere else.
207		want "$size: the full-screen display never came up" " Status "
208		want "$size: the full-screen display never came up" " Quadrant "
209	
210		unwanted "$size: paused with [HIT SPACE BAR] before asking anything" "HIT SPACE BAR"
211		unwanted "$size: paused with [CONTINUE?] before asking anything" "[CONTINUE?]"
212	
213		# With a pager waiting, its getch() swallowed the leading
214		# character and the game saw "egular".

Verify the change on branch `test/tui-ci-coverage` in /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek. It is **one uncommitted, test-only file**: `tests/tui.sh` (`git diff`). No game code is touched, and no CMake or CI change is needed — the branch is stacked on `fix/tui-first-keystroke` (PR #24, green, unmerged), which registered the test and installed tmux on both runners.

This closes issue #13, "Add TUI coverage to CI". Its acceptance criteria are:
- CI exercises `-t` in some form on at least Linux — already true via PR #24 (verified in the CI logs: `Test #6: tui ... Passed` on both Ubuntu and macOS).
- **No fixed-`sleep`-based races: 20 consecutive runs pass.**
- Failures produce useful diagnostics (captured pane content), not just a timeout.
- Bounded by a CTest `TIMEOUT` so a hang fails fast — `TIMEOUT 180`, and the test takes ~11s.

What this adds, on top of the existing first-run/paging/argv coverage:
- **panel liveness** — `warp 4` must move the Warp Factor field on the status panel. Without this the whole script would pass if the panels were painted once and never again.

## Failures

## Finding: one new assertion passes vacuously

`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tests/tui.sh:385`

```sh
want_re "replay: the quadrant panel is not showing a quadrant" "$QUADTITLE"
```

`QUADTITLE=' Quadrant [0-9]+ - [0-9]+ '` was chosen (per the comment at :142) so a bare `" Quadrant "` box label cannot satisfy it. It does that job — but in the *replay* case it is also satisfied by text the game leaves in the **message window**. `setup.c` ends the briefing with `cramlc(1, quadx, quady)` (which emits `" Quadrant 8 - 7"`) followed by `proutn(" ")`, giving:

```
 The Enterprise is currently in Quadrant 8 - 7  Sector 9 - 5
```

That is the third-from-last line still on screen at the `COMMAND>` prompt, so it always matches.

Proof, independently derived (mutant M3 = `tui.c:188` `mvwprintw(wquad, 0, 2, " Quadrant %d - %d ", quadx, quady);` deleted):

```
=========== m3 ===========
rc=1 in 10s
FAIL: thaw: the quadrant panel has no quadrant
```

Only the thaw assertion died. The replay one survived, and the probe dump confirms why — panel title reads bare ` Quadrant `, message window carries `Quadrant 8 - 7 `.

This is **deterministic**, not flaky (the briefing tail is always the last thing in the ten-line window). It does not make CI red; it means the replay case does not actually verify the quadrant panel is repopulated. The thaw case *is* real, because thawing prints `report(1)`, not the briefing — which is why the stated mutation battery, which only named the thaw assertion, did not catch this. The sibling `want "replay: the status panel is empty" "Stardate"` is genuinely load-bearing (the novice briefing says lowercase "It is stardate", and mutant M1 kills it).

| Round | Runs | Result | Wall time |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: idle (loadavg ~1) | 20 sequential | 20/20 pass | 10.7–11.5 s |
| B: 48 CPU hogs on 24 cores (loadavg 25→59) | 20 sequential | 20/20 pass | 12.2–19.5 s |
| C: ~250 CPU hogs + 6 copies of the script at once (loadavg 137) | 6 parallel | 6/6 pass | 16–17 s |

  Only reachable on a hang, which is already a failure, and CI runners are torn down anyway — but on a developer's box a timed-out run orphans a tmux server. I removed both artifacts I created.

1. The replay quadrant-panel assertion above — effectively no coverage that the quadrant panel repopulates for a second game.
2. Six failure sites produce **no pane dump**, so they would report a bare message rather than the captured screen the issue's acceptance criteria ask for: `tests/tui.sh:352, 371–372, 374–375, 414, 427–428, 457–458`. - No macOS host available, as above.

- Plain-mode piped journey (`regular/short/novice/xyz/srscan/quit/n/n`) — starts, accepts commands, exits 0, no `.trk`.

1	#!/bin/sh
2	# Drives the full-screen display through a real terminal.
3	#
4	# Everything else in the suite talks to the game through pipes, which
5	# reaches the no-terminal fallback but never exercises curses itself.
6	# This one runs the game inside tmux so there is a genuine pty, and
7	# reads the screen back the way a player would see it.
8	#
9	# It covers the ways into a running game -- answering the setup
10	# questions, giving the answers on the command line, thawing a saved
11	# game, and starting a second game after quitting -- because each of
12	# them arrives at the panels differently. It also covers the two
13	# refusals only a real terminal can produce: one curses cannot drive,
14	# and one too small for the panels. Both have to fall back to the
15	# classic display and keep playing.
16	#
17	# The size matters. 80x24 is what most terminal emulators open at and
18	# 72x24 is the smallest the TUI accepts; at both the message window is
19	# only ten lines, so the startup banner overflows it -- which is how
20	# the pager came to be waiting for a keystroke before the game had
21	# asked the player anything, and to eat the first letter of the answer.
22	#
23	# Usage: tui.sh /path/to/sst
24	# Exits 77 (ctest SKIP_RETURN_CODE) when there is no tmux to run in.
25	#
26	# Needs a sleep that takes a fraction, which GNU and BSD both have but
27	# POSIX does not promise; busybox would need whole seconds.
28	
29	set -u
30	
31	SST="${1:-./sst}"
32	case "$SST" in
33		/*) ;;
34		*) SST="$(pwd)/$SST" ;;
35	esac
36	srcdir=$(unset CDPATH; cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd)
37	
38	if ! command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1; then
39		# A developer without tmux gets a skip. CI does not: this is the
40		# only test that runs curses at all, and a green build that quietly
41		# skipped it would be worse than no test.
42		if [ -n "${CI:-}" ]; then
43			echo "FAIL: tmux is missing on CI, so the TUI went untested" >&2
44			exit 1
45		fi
46		echo "SKIP: tmux is not installed, so there is no pty to test in" >&2
47		exit 77
48	fi
49	if [ ! -x "$SST" ]; then
50		echo "FAIL: $SST is not executable" >&2
51		exit 1
52	fi
53	
54	# Run on a socket of our own, never the default one. A developer's tmux
55	# server is usually sitting on the default socket with a day's real work
56	# in it, and anything server-wide -- this script's cleanup, or an agent
57	# tidying up after driving the TUI by hand -- takes that down too. -L
58	# buys a private server, so cleanup can be as blunt as it needs to be.
59	socket="sst-tui-$$"
60	session="tui"
61	pane="$session:0.0"
62	
63	# -f /dev/null as well as -L: a private socket is not a private config,
64	# and `set -g base-index 1` -- one of the commoner things people put in
65	# ~/.tmux.conf -- moves the pane out from under the name used below, so
66	# every capture comes back empty and the game gets blamed for it.
67	tm() { tmux -f /dev/null -L "$socket" "$@"; }
68	
69	# tmux leaves the socket file behind when the server exits, so a suite
70	# that ran often would slowly fill the directory with dead ones. This is
71	# where tmux puts them on both Linux and macOS: $TMUX_TMPDIR if it is
72	# set, /tmp otherwise.
73	cleanup() {
74		tm kill-server 2>/dev/null
75		rm -f "${TMUX_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/tmux-$(id -u)/$socket"
76	}
77	
78	# The saved-game cases write a .trk file, which the game puts in the
79	# directory it is playing in. That must not be the source tree.
80	work=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/sst-tui.XXXXXX")
81	if [ -z "${work:-}" ] || [ ! -d "$work" ]; then
82		echo "FAIL: could not create a temporary directory" >&2
83		exit 1
84	fi
85	
86	finish() { cleanup; rm -rf "$work"; }
87	trap 'finish' EXIT
88	trap 'finish; exit 130' INT
89	trap 'finish; exit 143' TERM
90	trap 'finish; exit 129' HUP
91	
92	fails=0
93	fail() {
94		printf 'FAIL: %s\n' "$1" >&2
95		fails=$((fails + 1))
96	}
97	
98	screen() { tm capture-pane -t "$pane" -p 2>/dev/null; }
99	
100	dump() {
101		printf '  --- screen ---\n' >&2
102		screen | sed 's/^/  | /' >&2
103	}
104	
105	# Wait until the screen shows $1, up to about eight seconds. Polling
106	# beats a fixed sleep: curses paints in its own time, and a machine
107	# under load should not turn into a failure.
108	wait_for() {
109		i=0
110		while [ "$i" -lt 80 ]; do
111			if screen | grep -qF "$1"; then return 0; fi
112			i=$((i + 1))
113			sleep 0.1
114		done
115		return 1
116	}
117	
118	# Answer any paging prompts until the command prompt comes back. A
119	# space is only ever sent while a pause is actually showing, so this
120	# cannot quietly paper over a pause that should not have been there.
121	to_command() {
122		i=0
123		while [ "$i" -lt 40 ]; do
124			screen | grep -qF 'COMMAND' && return 0
125			if screen | grep -qE 'CONTINUE|HIT SPACE BAR'; then

128			i=$((i + 1))

130		done
131		return 1
132	}
133	
134	want() {
135		screen | grep -qF "$2" || { fail "$1"; dump; }
136	}
137	
138	# Wait for $2, or fail with $1 and the screen attached. Bare
139	# `wait_for ... || fail ...` reports the message and nothing else,
140	# which in a CI log is the least useful half of the story.
141	expect() {
142		wait_for "$2" || { fail "$1"; dump; }
143	}
144	
145	# The quadrant panel's title carries coordinates only while a game is
146	# set up; without one the box keeps its bare " Quadrant " label, so a
147	# fixed-string match for that would pass on the empty frame it is
148	# supposed to catch.
149	#
150	# Matched on the first line of the screen, which is where that border
151	# sits. Anywhere would also match the message window: the briefing ends
152	# by saying which quadrant the Enterprise is currently in, so an
153	# unanchored search passes even with the panel title gone.
154	want_quadtitle() {
155		screen | head -1 | grep -qE ' Quadrant [0-9]+ - [0-9]+ ' ||
156			{ fail "$1"; dump; }
157	}
158	
159	unwanted() {
160		if screen | grep -qF "$2"; then fail "$1"; dump; fi
161	}
162	
163	# Wait for $2 to leave the screen. A prompt is printed before the
164	# panels beside it are redrawn, so asking the instant the text appears
165	# can catch the previous game still framed for a few milliseconds --
166	# a race that would report a bug nobody has. Something that is meant to
167	# be gone goes within the timeout; something that is not, never does.
168	wait_gone() {
169		i=0
170		while [ "$i" -lt 40 ]; do
171			screen | grep -qF "$2" || return 0
172			i=$((i + 1))
173			sleep 0.1
174		done
175		fail "$1"
176		dump
177	}
178	
179	# tmux takes a shell command line, not an argument list, so the path
180	# has to survive being quoted into one.
181	sstq=$(printf "%s" "$SST" | sed "s/'/'\\\\''/g")
182	
183	# Start the game on a terminal $1 wide by $2 tall, passing $3 (if any)
184	# on the command line and running it under $4 (if any, an `env ...`
185	# prefix). It reads sst.doc from the current directory, and dies with
186	# the session.
187	startdir="$srcdir"	# where the game plays; sst.doc has to be here
188	start() {
189		cleanup
190		tm new-session -d -x "$1" -y "$2" -s "$session" -c "$startdir" \
191			"${4:-} '$sstq' -t ${3:-}; sleep 30" 2>/dev/null || {
192			echo "FAIL: could not start a ${1}x${2} tmux session" >&2
193			exit 1
194		}
195	}
196	
197	# --- the game asks before it pauses, at every size it accepts -------
198	# 80x24 is what most emulators open at; 72x24 is the smallest the TUI
199	# will run in. The banner is longer than the message window at both, so
200	# it scrolls -- ordinary. Stopping to ask for a keystroke is not:
201	# nothing has been asked yet, so there is no reader to wait for, and
202	# the prompt sits exactly where the player is about to type an answer.
203	for size in 80x24 72x24; do
204		cols=${size%x*}
205		rows=${size#*x}
206		start "$cols" "$rows"

208		if ! wait_for 'regular, tournament, or frozen'; then

212		fi

- **panel liveness** — `warp 4` must move the Warp Factor field. Without it the whole script would pass if the panels were painted once and never again.
- **replay** — quit → score questions → play again → second game; panels blank through the new game's setup, repopulated once it starts.
- **freeze/thaw** — `freeze sav`, restart with `frozen sav`; panels show the thawed game and its first command arrives whole. Played in a `mktemp -d`.
- **two refusals only a pty produces** — `TERM=dumb` and 70x20. Each prints its notice, draws no panels, and keeps playing in the classic display.

ui-review found: the quadrant-panel assertion was a fixed-string `"Quadrant "` match that the empty box label satisfies; the visible half of #21 was unasserted; and nothing checked the panels ever update. I deliberately assert nothing there and say so in a comment, since that is game behaviour and this is a test-only slice.

content.text:
## Verdict: request changes

Reviewed state: branch `test/tui-ci-coverage` at `d1c2cc5`, one uncommitted modification — `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tests/tui.sh` (+223/−11). Nothing staged, nothing untracked, no other file touched. I confirmed the branch diff vs `main` beyond this file is only the already-approved PR #24 content and did not re-review it.

The slice is well shaped and the new coverage is real — I independently reproduced two of the claimed mutation kills (deleting `setup.c:221` `tui_ingame = FALSE` fails exactly `"replay: the last game is still on the panels during setup"`; deleting `tui.c:188`'s quadrant-title `mvwprintw` fails exactly both quadrant assertions). But two of the new checks have a timing dependency of the same kind the change set out to remove, and both fixes are small.

### Findings

**1. should-fix — the four positive panel assertions are single-sample and race the panel repaint**
`tests/tui.sh:154-157` (`want_quadtitle`), `tests/tui.sh:394-395`, `tests/tui.sh:430-431`

`to_command` returns the moment `COMMAND` appears, but `sst.c:215` prints `COMMAND> ` and *then* calls `scan()` → `tui_readline()`, which is where `tui_refresh_panels()` runs (`tui.c:220`). For the first prompt of a replayed or thawed game the panels are still blank when the prompt is on screen — this is precisely the ordering the author documents in the `wait_gone` comment at `tests/tui.sh:163-167`, but the negative assertion polls and these four positive ones do not.

Measured, by injecting a stall at the top of `tui_refresh_panels()` in a scratch copy of the tree and running the unmodified script:

| injected stall | result |
|---|---|
| 8 ms | `tui OK` |
| 15 ms | `FAIL: replay: the quadrant panel is not showing a quadrant` |
| 30 ms | above + `FAIL: replay: the status panel is empty` |
| 200 ms | all four fail, 3/3 runs |

So a single ~15 ms scheduling stall in the game process between the prompt write and the repaint turns a green run red on a shared CI runner. Fix: give `want_quadtitle` the same poll loop as `wait_gone`, and change the two `want ... "Stardate"` calls to `expect` (the helper already added for exactly this). The mutants still die — they simply never draw the title, so the poll times out.

**2. should-fix — the freeze wait accepts a zero-byte save file, then kills the writer**
`tests/tui.sh:417-422`

The loop waits for `[ -f "$work/sav.trk" ]`, which is true from `fopen()` (`setup.c:42`). The payload is 3983 bytes — under `BUFSIZ`, so it is a single stdio flush that only happens at `fclose()`. The next statement is `start 80 24 'frozen sav'`, whose `cleanup` runs `tmux kill-server` and SIGHUPs the game. A stall between `fopen` and `fclose` leaves a truncated file; `thaw()` then reads nothing, `*passwd == 0` sends `choose()` back to its top (`setup.c:446`), and the run fails 10 s later as `"thaw: the thawed game never reached its prompt"` — a message that points at the wrong thing. Fix: `[ -s "$work/sav.trk" ]` at minimum, or better, prove the game is back at a prompt after freezing (send `lrscan`, wait for `Long-range scan for Quadrant`) before tearing the session down.

**3. nit — comment misstates what "yes" does**
`tests/tui.sh:361`: `Answered "no" deliberately: "yes" writes a score file.` Answering yes runs `chew2(); freeze(FALSE);` (`sst.c:491-497`): it writes a saved-game `.trk` *and* first prompts `File name(9 characters maximum): `, which would strand the test at an unexpected prompt. It also contradicts the accurate wording at `tests/tui.sh:304-306` ("would write a save file"). Say "writes a save file and stops to ask for its name".

**4. nit — comment claims a comparison the script does not make**
`tests/tui.sh:373-374`: "A different assignment clears it here than the one that cleared it above, so both are worth asking about." Only `setup.c:221` is exercised; the other clearing assignment (`finish.c:74`) is never reached in this script — as the comment at `355-359` itself explains — and nothing above asserts the panels were cleared. Reword or drop.

**5. nit — the liveness assertion depends on the generated galaxy**
`tests/tui.sh:334-341`. `warp 4` in the `tournament 5 long emeritus` game: if that seed puts the Enterprise in a Romulan neutral zone, `setup()` runs `attack(0)` (`setup.c:415`) and `setwarp` refuses with "Warp engines inoperative" once `damage[DWARPEN] > 10`, leaving the panel at 5.0 and failing as `"the status panel did not follow the game"`. Linux is fine; macOS `rand()` gives a different galaxy and has never run this case. Low probability and the dump makes it diagnosable, but a novice/short game — or asserting the command was accepted before asserting the panel moved — would remove the dependency.

**6. nit — the 70x20 notice check depends on the pane not scrolling**
`tests/tui.sh:453`. I measured the actual screen: notice + banner = 16 lines, question on line 17, in 20 rows — so the comment at `471-474` is exactly right today, with three lines of slack. `screen`-with-history (`capture-pane -S -`) for just this one `wait_for` would make it immune to a future line added to `prelim()`. Optional.

### Verified clean

But two of the new checks have a timing dependency of the same kind the change set out to remove, and both fixes are small.

### Findings

**1. should-fix — the four positive panel assertions are single-sample and race the panel repaint**
`tests/tui.sh:154-157` (`want_quadtitle`), `tests/tui.sh:394-395`, `tests/tui.sh:430-431`

`to_command` returns the moment `COMMAND` appears, but `sst.c:215` prints `COMMAND> ` and *then* calls `scan()` → `tui_readline()`, which is where `tui_refresh_panels()` runs (`tui.c:220`). For the first prompt of a replayed or thawed game the panels are still blank when the prompt is on screen — this is precisely the ordering the author documents in the `wait_gone` comment at `tests/tui.sh:163-167`, but the negative assertion polls and these four positive ones do not.

Measured, by injecting a stall at the top of `tui_refresh_panels()` in a scratch copy of the tree and running the unmodified script:

| injected stall | result |
|---|---|
| 8 ms | `tui OK` |
| 15 ms | `FAIL: replay: the quadrant panel is not showing a quadrant` |
| 30 ms | above + `FAIL: replay: the status panel is empty` |
| 200 ms | all four fail, 3/3 runs |

So a single ~15 ms scheduling stall in the game process between the prompt write and the repaint turns a green run red on a shared CI runner. Fix: give `want_quadtitle` the same poll loop as `wait_gone`, and change the two `want ... "Stardate"` calls to `expect` (the helper already added for exactly this). The mutants still die — they simply never draw the title, so the poll times out.

**2. should-fix — the freeze wait accepts a zero-byte save file, then kills the writer**
`tests/tui.sh:417-422`

The loop waits for `[ -f "$work/sav.trk" ]`, which is true from `fopen()` (`setup.c:42`). The payload is 3983 bytes — under `BUFSIZ`, so it is a single stdio flush that only happens at `fclose()`. The next statement is `start 80 24 'frozen sav'`, whose `cleanup` runs `tmux kill-server` and SIGHUPs the game. A stall between `fopen` and `fclose` leaves a truncated file; `thaw()` then reads nothing, `*passwd == 0` sends `choose()` back to its top (`setup.c:446`), and the run fails 10 s later as `"thaw: the thawed game never reached its prompt"` — a message that points at the wrong thing. Fix: `[ -s "$work/sav.trk" ]` at minimum, or better, prove the game is back at a prompt after freezing (send `lrscan`, wait for `Long-range scan for Quadrant`) before tearing the session down.

**3. nit — comment misstates what "yes" does**
`tests/tui.sh:361`: `Answered "no" deliberately: "yes" writes a score file.` Answering yes runs `chew2(); freeze(FALSE);` (`sst.c:491-497`): it writes a saved-game `.trk` *and* first prompts `File name(9 characters maximum): `, which would strand the test at an unexpected prompt. It also contradicts the accurate wording at `tests/tui.sh:304-306` ("would write a save file"). Say "writes a save file and stops to ask for its name".

**4. nit — comment claims a comparison the script does not make**
`tests/tui.sh:373-374`: "A different assignment clears it here than the one that cleared it above, so both are worth asking about." Only `setup.c:221` is exercised; the other clearing assignment (`finish.c:74`) is never reached in this script — as the comment at `355-359` itself explains — and nothing above asserts the panels were cleared. Reword or drop.

**5. nit — the liveness assertion depends on the generated galaxy**
`tests/tui.sh:334-341`. `warp 4` in the `tournament 5 long emeritus` game: if that seed puts the Enterprise in a Romulan neutral zone, `setup()` runs `attack(0)` (`setup.c:415`) and `setwarp` refuses with "Warp engines inoperative" once `damage[DWARPEN] > 10`, leaving the panel at 5.0 and failing as `"the status panel did not follow the game"`. Linux is fine; macOS `rand()` gives a different galaxy and has never run this case. Low probability and the dump makes it diagnosable, but a novice/short game — or asserting the command was accepted before asserting the panel moved — would remove the dependency.

**6. nit — the 70x20 notice check depends on the pane not scrolling**
`tests/tui.sh:453`. I measured the actual screen: notice + banner = 16 lines, question on line 17, in 20 rows — so the comment at `471-474` is exactly right today, with three lines of slack. `screen`-with-history (`capture-pane -S -`) for just this one `wait_for` would make it immune to a future line added to `prelim()`. # Everything above would still pass if the panels were painted once and
# never again, which is most of what the full-screen display is for.
# Warp factor is the cheapest thing to change: it moves a status field
# and nothing else -- no time passes, nothing shoots back.
if [ -n "$argv_ok" ]; then
	want "the warp factor is not on the status panel" "Warp Factor   5.0"
	tm send-keys -t "$pane" 'warp 4' Enter
	if ! wait_for "Warp Factor   4.0"; then
		fail "the status panel did not follow the game"
		dump
	fi
fi

# --- a second game gets its own panels -------------------------------
# Carrying the same session on through quit and into a replay. The
# panels are wired to a flag that says a game is set up; getting that
# wrong showed the next player the last player's quadrant, or an empty
# frame around a game that was running (#21).
replay_case() {
	tm send-keys -t "$pane" 'quit' Enter
	if ! wait_for 'score recorded'; then
		fail "replay: quit did not reach the end-of-game questions"
		dump
		return
	fi
	# Nothing is asserted about the panels here: `quit` sets alldone
	# by hand rather than going through finish(), so it never clears
	# the flag, and the game you just left stays framed behind these
	# questions. finish() blanks them deliberately -- the two paths
	# disagree, but that is the game's business, not this test's.
	#
	# Answered "no" deliberately: "yes" writes a score file.
	tm send-keys -t "$pane" 'n' Enter
	expect "replay: never asked about another game" 'play again'
	tm send-keys -t "$pane" 'y' Enter
	if ! wait_for 'regular, tournament, or frozen'; then
		fail "replay: the second game never started"
		dump
		return
	fi
	# And still blank through the second game's setup questions, which
	# is where the last captain's quadrant used to be framed above
	# someone else's answers (#21). A different assignment clears it
	# here than the one that cleared it above, so both are worth
	# asking about.
	wait_gone "replay: the last game is still on the panels during setup" "Stardate"
	# No banner this time, so nothing has overflowed the window -- but
	# the pager stays armed from the first game, and a pause here
	# would eat this answer just the same.
	unwanted "replay: paused before the second game's first question" "CONTINUE"

	tm send-keys -t "$pane" 'regular' Enter
	expect "replay: the second game lost the first answer" 'Short, Medium, or Long'
	tm send-keys -t "$pane" 'short' Enter
	expect "replay: setup did not reach the skill question" 'Novice, Fair, Good, Expert'
	tm send-keys -t "$pane" 'novice' Enter
	sleep 0.5
	tm send-keys -t "$pane" 'xyz' Enter
	if ! to_command; then
		fail "replay: the second game never reached its prompt"
		dump
		return
	fi
	# And back on for the new one.
	want_quadtitle "replay: the quadrant panel is not showing a quadrant"
	want "replay: the status panel is empty" "Stardate"
}

# Only if there is a game to quit out of; otherwise 'quit' goes into
# whatever prompt is up and buries the real failure in noise.

## Verdict: approve

Reviewed state: branch `test/tui-ci-coverage` at commit `d1c2cc5` plus the two uncommitted files — `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tests/tui.sh` (modified) and `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/CMakeLists.txt` (modified). Per your instruction I re-reviewed only the five deltas, not the rest of the branch diff vs `main`.

### Verification I ran

**Nit 1 — `cut -c30-` lands on the status panel.** `tui.c:157-159` gives `QUADW 29`, so `wquad` owns 0-based columns 0-28 and `wstat` starts at 0-based 29 = 1-based 30, independent of `COLS`. Confirmed empirically on a private socket at both sizes: at 80x24 and 72x24 `cut -c30-` starts exactly on the status panel's left border, and `index($0,"Stardate")` is 32 in both. Message-window rows (`wmsg` at x=1, no box) survive the cut only past screen column 30.

Vacuity checked against every in-tree `Stardate` producer: `reports.c:338` (`srscan`'s right-hand column) puts it at screen column 27 — cut leaves `date  …`, no match; `setup.c:393` and `reports.c:11/19` are at columns 2 and 24. Only `events.c:656` ("Message from Starfleet Command       Stardate ") reaches column 39, and that needs an `events()` firing, i.e. elapsed game time, which neither assertion point has.

Liveness confirmed by mutation: `tuifmt.c:112` `"Stardate      %.1f"` → `"Sardate       %.1f"` yields exactly `replay: the status panel is empty` and `thaw: the panels are not showing the thawed game`, and nothing else. So the confined match is neither vacuous nor over-broad.

(Multibyte aside: this tmux emits ACS as single-byte fallback, so bytes == columns. Even where tmux emits UTF-8 box drawing, GNU `cut -c` counting bytes only shifts the cut a couple of bytes left *on panel rows* — into the quadrant grid, which never says "Stardate" — and message rows are pure ASCII, so the confinement holds either way.)

**Nit 2 — `LRSCAN` regex.** `reports.c:118-135` confirms the two alternatives are the only outputs of an accepted/refused `lrscan` in the reachable states, and `sst.c:245-247` confirms a truncated command gets `UNRECOGNIZED COMMAND.`, which matches neither. Both issues filed, and **#13 is done, pushed, and green — including on macOS.**

**Filed:** [#25](https://github.com/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/issues/25) (briefing and score never page — `proutf`'s embedded newlines don't increment `linecount`) and [#26](https://github.com/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/issues/26) (make the banner fit 80x24, tagged good-first-issue).

**[PR #27](https://github.com/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/pull/27)**, commit `c02b78e`, signed. Stacked on #24, so **#24 merges first** and #27 retargets to `main` automatically.

The residual risk I flagged is now closed: `Test #6: tui ... Passed 16.67 sec` on the macOS runner, which is the first time freeze/thaw, replay, liveness and both fallback paths have ever executed there.

**The finding that mattered most** wasn't in the issue: nothing checked the panels *ever change*. Every assertion in the file — the ones #24 shipped included — would have passed on a display painted once and never again, which is most of what `-t` is for. That's now `warp 4` moving the Warp Factor field.

The review rounds were unusually productive here, and all three caught the same species of defect — a check that cannot fail:

1. ui-review: the quadrant assertion was a fixed-string `"Quadrant "`, which the *empty* box label satisfies.
2. verifier: the replacement regex was unanchored, and the briefing's own "currently in Quadrant 8 - 7" satisfies it from the message window — so it still passed with the panel title deleted.
3. code-review: the four positive panel checks sampled once and raced the repaint; it measured the window by injecting a stall, and 15ms was enough to turn a green run red.

Six mutations of the panel wiring now each die at the assertion meant for them. 20/20 consecutive runs locally, 46/46 for the verifier under load.

One thing I deliberately did **not** assert, and it may be worth an issue: after `quit`, the panels keep showing the game you just left through the score questions. `quit` sets `alldone` by hand instead of going through `finish()`, which is the only path that clears the flag — and `finish()` clears it deliberately, with a comment about letting the epilogue have the screen. The two paths disagree. It's defensible either way, so I left it as game behaviour rather than encoding my guess into a test.

content.text:
All merged. `main` is at `19315ca`, working tree clean, 7/7 tests green, no open PRs.

```
19315ca test(tui): cover the full-screen display through a real terminal (#28)
70932af fix(tui): stop the pager eating the player's first keystroke (#24)
191ed5b feat(tui): colour the quadrant grid and the status panel (#23)
```

One wrinkle worth knowing about: merging #24 with `--delete-branch` **closed #27**, because it was stacked on that branch and GitHub won't reopen a PR whose base is gone. I rebased the branch onto the squashed `main` (dropping the already-merged commit), re-ran CI, and landed it as #28. Same commit, same content — just a different number than the one I quoted you earlier.

## Where things stand

The TUI is now essentially finished as a feature. Over this session it went from "renders panels" to: colour, CRLF-safe help, non-tty and terminfo fallbacks, correct behaviour at the 72x24 floor, EOF handling, and a pty-driven test that runs on both CI platforms and is mutation-proven. **The `-t` flag is now the best-tested part of the codebase.**

Which is also the problem.

## What's next

Eight issues, and they fall into two clearly different piles.

**Player-facing TUI gaps** — #25 (briefing and score scroll away unread), #26 (banner fit, good-first-issue), #8 (indicate *why* the grid is masked), #9 (resize).

**Engineering debt** — #12 (seeded journey over movement, combat, docking), #14 (clear warnings, then `-Werror`), #10 (osx.c header, good-first-issue), #15 (dead `main.c`, Windows docs).

My recommendation is **#25 next, then #12.**

#25 because it's the only open bug, it's the very next screen a new player sees after the banner I just fixed, and the reasoning is already loaded — it's the same `linecount`/`skip()` machinery, with the twist that `proutf()`'s embedded newlines bypass the counter entirely. The constraint that makes it non-trivial is that the naive fix (count newlines in `proutf`) changes paging everywhere, including plain mode at its 23-line threshold.

#12 because of the imbalance above: the suite now covers I/O plumbing and the display thoroughly, and the *game* — combat, movement, docking, events — essentially not at all. Every refactor in the other pile, #14 especially, is riskier than it needs to be until that exists.

One more candidate worth filing, from the #13 review: `quit` sets `alldone` by hand instead of going through `finish()`, so it never clears `tui_ingame` and the game you just left stays framed behind the score questions — while `finish()` blanks the panels deliberately, with a comment about letting the epilogue have the screen. The two paths disagree. I left it alone rather than encode a guess about which is right; say the word and I'll file it.

input.prompt:
Review the change on branch `fix/tui-briefing-paging` in /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek. Uncommitted: `sst.c` and `tests/tui.sh` (`git diff`).

Context — issue #25: text printed with an embedded `\n` never counted towards paging, because `proutf()` formatted into a buffer and handed the whole blob to `proutn()`, while only `skip()` increments `linecount`. So the two longest passages in the game scrolled away unread in the ten-line TUI message window: the mission briefing (the only place the game states the mission and the deadline, and at novice skill the tutorial) and the end-of-game score table.

The fix: `proutf()` now prints its buffer a line at a time — `proutn()` for the text, `skip(1)` at each newline — so those newlines page like any others. Deliberately not conditional on the display.

**Consequences I want your judgement on:**

1. **Plain mode changes**, narrowly. Measured over 27 seeded journeys: `short novice` and `medium good` gain no pauses at all; `long emeritus` gains exactly one, in 3 of 9 games — the briefing there genuinely exceeds plain mode's 23-line threshold. Is a plain-mode player being asked to press a key during setup acceptable, given the alternative is text scrolling off a 24-line terminal?

2. **The briefing still scrolls away when setup answers come from the command line** (`sst -t tournament 9 short novice pw`). That is #17's gate working as designed: the player has not typed yet, so a pause there would eat the first character of their first command. Right call, or does it need something else?

3. **The score table is not directly tested.** A populated score needs a played-out game (kills, casualties), which is issue #12's territory — `quit` alone prints only the `****` rule and the score question. The mechanism is shared with the briefing, which is tested. Is that an acceptable place to draw the line?

Please play it and judge the result as an expert in games and CLI games — does the briefing now read the way it should, is the pause in the right place, is anything else in the game newly interrupted that shouldn't be?

Testing needs a pty. Use tmux **on your own socket via `-L <unique>` and `-f /dev/null`**, never the default socket, never a bare `kill-server`, never `kill-session` on a session you did not create. Never redirect the game's stdout in a tmux session. Build is at ./build. Check 80x24 and 72x24. Remove any `*.trk` you leave in the repo root.

Report findings only; do not edit files.

content.text:
Cleaned up: my tmux server (`-L sstrev`) killed, my baseline worktree removed, no `.trk` left in the repo, no files modified.

## Verdict

**Acceptable as-is.** The fix does exactly what it claims and the result reads the way the briefing should: at 80x24 and 72x24 the game now stops after the mission statement and the deadline, the player presses space, and the rest of the briefing (starbases, position, "Good Luck!") arrives on a second page with nothing lost. On the same terminal the pre-fix binary drops the player straight at `COMMAND>` showing only the last four lines — I ran both side by side to confirm. Nothing else in the game is newly interrupted: `srscan`, `chart`, `help move` and the self-destruct countdown page at exactly the same points as before, and `lrscan` — whose three row-terminating `proutf("\n")` newly count — gains no pause because `linecount` resets at each `COMMAND>`. My findings are all about how the change is described and where it doesn't reach, not about the change itself.

## Answers to your three questions

**1. Plain mode — yes, acceptable, but the measurement needs a build type attached.** In `short novice` the added pause lands precisely on the right beat: after "Good Luck!", at the end of the briefing, before the first `COMMAND>`. That is the classic sst behaviour and a plain-mode player pressing space there is losing nothing.

The caveat: your `long emeritus` figure looks like it was measured in a Debug build. `setup.c:285/291` prints `DEBUG: Abandoning base #N at x-y` unconditionally under `#ifdef DEBUG` (not gated on `idebug`), and those lines go through `proutf` with a trailing `\n` — so they only started counting towards paging with this change. Seeds 1-12 at `long emeritus`: Debug build pauses on seed 5, Release build pauses on none of the twelve. Worth restating in the commit as "3 of 9 in a Debug build", or re-measuring against Release, otherwise the number isn't reproducible for anyone building the way a player would.

Second caveat, for future test authors rather than for this change: the plain-mode pause reads from stdin, so a piped journey that trips it loses one character. `printf 'tournament 3 short novice pw\n…'` hits it today.

**2. The command-line path — right call, but record the cost.** `./build/sst -t regular short novice pw` at 80x24 leaves the player at `COMMAND>` looking at:

```
 your mission.  As you proceed you may be given more time.
 You will have 2 supporting starbases.
 Starbase locations-   4 - 7   4 - 8
 The Enterprise is currently in Quadrant 6 - 3  Sector 7 - 6
 Good Luck!
```

No mission, no deadline, and at novice no tutorial. That is the documented shortcut giving a strictly worse first screen than answering the questions — the one place the fix doesn't reach. I'd keep the gate (the keystroke-eating failure is worse) but soften the loss one of two ways: treat the command-line case as `prompted` on the grounds that the player demonstrably pressed Enter in their shell and is watching, not mid-answer (risk is type-ahead only); or leave the gate alone and make the mission recoverable — `report` currently restates skill, length, Klingons and bases but never the deadline, and the Status panel's "Time Left" is the only surviving trace of it.

**3. Score table — reasonable line, but slightly overstated.** A populated table doesn't need a played-out game: `destruct` plus the password ends it in two commands and yields a real table ("1 ship lost or destroyed", "Penalty for getting yourself killed", plus anything the blast kills — in `tournament 5 long emeritus` it also caught a Romulan). I drove that to completion in the TUI at 72x24 on both binaries and watched the new build page the endgame where the old one printed the whole thing in one blast. What that *doesn't* give you is a table long enough to need two pages, which is fair — so "the mechanism is covered by the briefing" holds. I'd file the destruct route as a cheap follow-up test, not a blocker.

## Findings

1. **(nit) Debug-build traces now cost a whole pager page** — `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/setup.c:285` and `:291`. At `long emeritus` in the documented Debug build, the player's first page is five `DEBUG: Abandoning base #3 at 8-4` lines plus `Stardate 2000.`, then `[CONTINUE?]`. Before this change that noise scrolled by uncounted; now it earns a stop. Suggest gating both on the existing `idebug` flag (`if (idebug) proutf(...)`), which is what the password `debug` already exists for.

2. **(nit) The new assertion only runs at 72x24** — `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tests/tui.sh:319`. It sits after the `for size in 80x24 72x24` loop, so it carries on from the 72-column game only. The bug is width-independent, but the comment block above the loop makes a point of checking both sizes; either move the briefing check inside the loop or say why 72 is the one that matters.

3. **(nit) The assertion doesn't prove the pause held, or that the tail survived** — same file. `expect ... 'The Federation is being attacked by'` passes if the opening is on screen for any reason; the neighbouring `help move` case does it more strongly with a `sleep 0.5` plus `want ... "CONTINUE"`. Consider adding the same two-step here, and a `want` for `Good Luck!` after `to_command` so the test also states that the second half is still reachable rather than only that the first half stopped.

4. **(nit, pre-existing, not caused by this change)** At 72 columns `REMEMBER--The score doesn't really matter until the mission is accomplished!` and the death banner `************ Entropy of Enterprise maximized *********` both wrap mid-word in the message window. Unchanged by this branch; mentioning it only so it isn't mistaken for fallout later.

## What I exercised

- Read the diff, `sst.c`'s `skip()`/`pause()`/`proutn()`/`proutf()`, `setup.c`'s briefing, `reports.c` `lrscan`/`chart`/`srscan`, `finish.c` `score()`, and `tests/tui.sh`.
- Built the branch Debug and Release; built a baseline worktree at `19315ca` for side-by-side comparison, then removed it.
- Plain mode, seeded (`tournament N`) diffs of branch vs baseline across `short novice`, `medium good`, `long emeritus`, seeds 1-12/42/99, in both Debug and Release, with `srscan lrscan chart status damages report quit`.

content.text:
Cleaned up: my tmux server (`-L sstrev`) killed, my baseline worktree removed, no `.trk` left in the repo, no files modified.

## Verdict

**Acceptable as-is.** The fix does exactly what it claims and the result reads the way the briefing should: at 80x24 and 72x24 the game now stops after the mission statement and the deadline, the player presses space, and the rest of the briefing (starbases, position, "Good Luck!") arrives on a second page with nothing lost. On the same terminal the pre-fix binary drops the player straight at `COMMAND>` showing only the last four lines — I ran both side by side to confirm. Nothing else in the game is newly interrupted: `srscan`, `chart`, `help move` and the self-destruct countdown page at exactly the same points as before, and `lrscan` — whose three row-terminating `proutf("\n")` newly count — gains no pause because `linecount` resets at each `COMMAND>`. My findings are all about how the change is described and where it doesn't reach, not about the change itself.

## Answers to your three questions

**1. Plain mode — yes, acceptable, but the measurement needs a build type attached.** In `short novice` the added pause lands precisely on the right beat: after "Good Luck!", at the end of the briefing, before the first `COMMAND>`. That is the classic sst behaviour and a plain-mode player pressing space there is losing nothing.

The caveat: your `long emeritus` figure looks like it was measured in a Debug build. `setup.c:285/291` prints `DEBUG: Abandoning base #N at x-y` unconditionally under `#ifdef DEBUG` (not gated on `idebug`), and those lines go through `proutf` with a trailing `\n` — so they only started counting towards paging with this change. Seeds 1-12 at `long emeritus`: Debug build pauses on seed 5, Release build pauses on none of the twelve. Worth restating in the commit as "3 of 9 in a Debug build", or re-measuring against Release, otherwise the number isn't reproducible for anyone building the way a player would.

Second caveat, for future test authors rather than for this change: the plain-mode pause reads from stdin, so a piped journey that trips it loses one character. `printf 'tournament 3 short novice pw\n…'` hits it today.

**2. The command-line path — right call, but record the cost.** `./build/sst -t regular short novice pw` at 80x24 leaves the player at `COMMAND>` looking at:

```
 your mission.  As you proceed you may be given more time.
 You will have 2 supporting starbases.
 Starbase locations-   4 - 7   4 - 8
 The Enterprise is currently in Quadrant 6 - 3  Sector 7 - 6
 Good Luck!
```

No mission, no deadline, and at novice no tutorial. That is the documented shortcut giving a strictly worse first screen than answering the questions — the one place the fix doesn't reach. I'd keep the gate (the keystroke-eating failure is worse) but soften the loss one of two ways: treat the command-line case as `prompted` on the grounds that the player demonstrably pressed Enter in their shell and is watching, not mid-answer (risk is type-ahead only); or leave the gate alone and make the mission recoverable — `report` currently restates skill, length, Klingons and bases but never the deadline, and the Status panel's "Time Left" is the only surviving trace of it.

**3. Score table — reasonable line, but slightly overstated.** A populated table doesn't need a played-out game: `destruct` plus the password ends it in two commands and yields a real table ("1 ship lost or destroyed", "Penalty for getting yourself killed", plus anything the blast kills — in `tournament 5 long emeritus` it also caught a Romulan). I drove that to completion in the TUI at 72x24 on both binaries and watched the new build page the endgame where the old one printed the whole thing in one blast. What that *doesn't* give you is a table long enough to need two pages, which is fair — so "the mechanism is covered by the briefing" holds. I'd file the destruct route as a cheap follow-up test, not a blocker.

## Findings

1. **(nit) Debug-build traces now cost a whole pager page** — `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/setup.c:285` and `:291`. At `long emeritus` in the documented Debug build, the player's first page is five `DEBUG: Abandoning base #3 at 8-4` lines plus `Stardate 2000.`, then `[CONTINUE?]`. Before this change that noise scrolled by uncounted; now it earns a stop. Suggest gating both on the existing `idebug` flag (`if (idebug) proutf(...)`), which is what the password `debug` already exists for.

2. **(nit) The new assertion only runs at 72x24** — `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tests/tui.sh:319`. It sits after the `for size in 80x24 72x24` loop, so it carries on from the 72-column game only. The bug is width-independent, but the comment block above the loop makes a point of checking both sizes; either move the briefing check inside the loop or say why 72 is the one that matters.

3. **(nit) The assertion doesn't prove the pause held, or that the tail survived** — same file. `expect ... 'The Federation is being attacked by'` passes if the opening is on screen for any reason; the neighbouring `help move` case does it more strongly with a `sleep 0.5` plus `want ... "CONTINUE"`. Consider adding the same two-step here, and a `want` for `Good Luck!` after `to_command` so the test also states that the second half is still reachable rather than only that the first half stopped.

4. **(nit, pre-existing, not caused by this change)** At 72 columns `REMEMBER--The score doesn't really matter until the mission is accomplished!` and the death banner `************ Entropy of Enterprise maximized *********` both wrap mid-word in the message window. Unchanged by this branch; mentioning it only so it isn't mistaken for fallout later.

## What I exercised

- Read the diff, `sst.c`'s `skip()`/`pause()`/`proutn()`/`proutf()`, `setup.c`'s briefing, `reports.c` `lrscan`/`chart`/`srscan`, `finish.c` `score()`, and `tests/tui.sh`.
- Built the branch Debug and Release; built a baseline worktree at `19315ca` for side-by-side comparison, then removed it.
- Plain mode, seeded (`tournament N`) diffs of branch vs baseline across `short novice`, `medium good`, `long emeritus`, seeds 1-12/42/99, in both Debug and Release, with `srscan lrscan chart status damages report quit`.
- Plain mode end-of-game with a populated score table via `destruct` (`tournament 5 long emeritus`); exactly one added pause, before the table.
- TUI via tmux on socket `sstrev` with `-f /dev/null`, at both 80x24 and 72x24, branch and baseline: interactive setup and the full briefing at novice and at emeritus; `srscan`, `lrscan` ×2, `chart`, `status`, `damages`, `report`, `score`, `shields up`, `phasers 500`, `move 1 2` (galactic-barrier warning and `[ANNOUNCEMENT ARRIVING...]`), Romulan neutral-zone attack, full self-destruct sequence through the death banner, score table and the record/play-again prompts.
- TUI command-line-args path `-t regular short novice pw` at 80x24.
- `ctest --test-dir build` — 7/7 pass. `tests/tui.sh` against the baseline binary — fails with `FAIL: the briefing scrolled past its opening`, exit 1, i.e. the new check genuinely catches the bug.

**Issue #25.** Text printed with an embedded `\n` never counted towards paging: `proutf()` formatted into a buffer and handed the whole blob to `proutn()`, while only `skip()` increments `linecount`. `tests/tui.sh` gains: the briefing's opening line must be on screen after setup, the pause must still be holding half a second later, and `Good Luck!` must be reachable after answering it — so the test states that the first half stops *and* the second half survives.

- **Debug plain mode, no `debug` password:** differs from `main` only by the absence of the now-gated trace lines; no paging change.

content.text:
Cleanup done, repo untouched (`git status` shows only the three intended modified files; the stray `n.trk` I generated has been removed).

# Verdict: FAIL

Nothing is broken — all builds, all 7 ctest tests, and every journey pass. It fails on one thing: **the "Release plain mode is byte-identical to `main`" measurement is wrong**, and the counterexamples point at a sibling of the exact bug the `setup.c` half of this diff fixes.

---

## 1. The `proutf` rewrite itself is correct (item 1)

I linked the real `proutf` from both `main` and the branch into a harness (`/tmp/.../scratchpad/harness.c`, built against every game source with `-Dmain=sst_real_main`) and diffed the raw bytes with `prompted == FALSE`, so paging is out of the picture and only the splitting logic is under test:

| case | input | result |
|---|---|---|
| trailing `\n` | `"abc\n"` | identical |
| no `\n` | `"xyz"` | identical |
| empty result | `proutf("%s","")` | identical (nothing emitted) |
| consecutive `\n\n` | `"a\n\nb\n"` | identical, two skips |
| leading `\n` | `"\nlead"` | identical |
| only `\n` | `"\n"` | identical |
| interior only | `"one\ntwo\nthree"` | identical |
| **truncation** | 1100-char string, `\n` every 100 | identical — `vsnprintf` cuts at 511, the mid-line tail goes out via the final `proutn` with no newline, exactly as before |

`cmp` on the two capture files: **byte-identical**. The in-place `*nl = '\0'` mutation is safe (`buf` is `proutf`'s own automatic), and truncation cannot lose or invent a newline relative to the old code.

## 2. No bad recursion (item 2)

`skip()` only ever calls `pause(0)`. `pause(0)` uses `proutn` exclusively (`"\n"`, `"[CONTINUE?]"` / `"[HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]"`, `"\r ... \r"`), never `proutf`/`prout`/`skip`, does not `clearscreen()` (that is gated on `i != 0`), and zeroes `linecount` on exit. `pause(1)` — the only path that calls `prout` and so re-enters `skip` — is never reached from `skip`. `getch()` (`osx.c:33`) handles EOF by returning `'\0'`, so a proutf-triggered pause at end of input cannot hang. No recursion, verified by the 320 journeys below completing with `rc=0`.

## 3. FAILURE — Release plain mode is *not* byte-identical (item 5)

```
# 320 seeded journeys: 16 seeds x {short-novice, long-emeritus, short-expert, long-good} x 5 command mixes
ls scratchpad/cases/*.in | xargs -P 12 -I{} scratchpad/one2.sh \
    scratchpad/v3/base/br/sst  build-release/sst  scratchpad/cmprel3 {}
```
**312 OK, 8 DIFF**, all Release, all deterministic (3 reruns each → 3/3 DIFF; baseline-vs-baseline on the same 8 → 8/8 OK, so it is not nondeterminism):

```
0187 42-emeritus-long-1     0268 1234-emeritus-long-2
0247 777-emeritus-long-1    0270 1234-emeritus-long-4
0267 1234-emeritus-long-1   0272 1234-expert-short-1
                            0273 1234-expert-short-2 / 0275 1234-expert-short-4
```

Example (`diff a-0267.txt b-0267.txt`) — a pause that did not exist on `main`:
```
89c89
< 
---
> [CONTINUE?]                           
```
In 4 of the 8 the pause count goes 0 → 1 (a new keypress an interactive plain-mode player must now make); in the other 4 an existing pause moves. Stripping the pause prompts makes the text md5s match, so no text is lost — it is purely paging.

**Root cause, confirmed by experiment.** Every one of the 8 is a combat journey containing `Hit <n> energy <n>` lines. `battle.c:642`

```c
proutf("Hit %g energy %g\n", hit, energy);
```

is an ungated debug trace — not `if (idebug)`, **not even inside `#ifdef DEBUG`** — that prints in Release on every enemy hit. I deleted that one line from *both* binaries, rebuilt, and reran the 8 cases: **8/8 OK**. It is the sole cause of the Release plain-mode change.

input.prompt:
Review branch `fix/tui-briefing-paging` in /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek — the working-tree diff (`git diff`) plus every staged/untracked file. Uncommitted: `sst.c`, `setup.c`, `battle.c`, `tests/journey.sh`, `tests/tui.sh`. `main` is at `19315ca`.

Act as an expert in C, POSIX shell and terminal games.

**Issue #25.** Text printed with an embedded `\n` never counted towards paging: `proutf()` formatted into a buffer and handed the whole blob to `proutn()`, while only `skip()` increments `linecount`. So the mission briefing — the only place the game states the mission and the deadline, and at novice skill the tutorial — scrolled away unread in the ten-line TUI message window, leaving the player at `COMMAND>` looking at its last four lines.

**The change:**
1. `sst.c` — `proutf()` prints its buffer a line at a time (`proutn()` for text, `skip(1)` at each newline). Not conditional on the display, deliberately.
2. `setup.c`, `battle.c` — four developer diagnostics that printed unasked are now behind the existing `idebug` flag (the `debug` password). Two in `setup.c` printed in every Debug build; **`battle.c:642` (`"Hit %g energy %g\n"`) printed in every build including Release, on every enemy hit** — it was not even inside `#ifdef DEBUG`. Once `proutf` counts newlines, this noise costs the player whole pages, which is how it was found.
3. `tests/tui.sh` — the briefing's opening must be on screen after setup, the pause must still be holding half a second later, and `Good Luck!` must be reachable after answering it.
4. `tests/journey.sh` — no build may print developer chatter to a player who did not ask; the `DEBUG:` check that was Release-only now applies to every build type, plus a combat-diagnostic check.

**Verifier findings, both addressed:** it proved the `proutf` rewrite byte-identical to the old one across nine edge cases (truncation mid-line, trailing/leading/only/consecutive newlines, empty result) using a linked harness, and confirmed no bad recursion (`skip` → `pause(0)` uses only `proutn`). It then **failed the branch** for a false claim of mine — that Release plain mode was byte-identical — tracing 8 diffs to `battle.c:642`. That is what part 2 above now fixes.

**Measurements after the fix:**
- **Release: 0 diffs over 39 seeded journeys including combat**, comparing against `main` with the now-gated `Hit … energy` line removed. 9 of those journeys emitted it on `main`.
- Debug: identical except the traces now need the `debug` password.
- No paging change for players in either build type.
- `tests/tui.sh` 20/20; 7/7 ctest in Debug and Release; the new assertions produce 3 failures against a `main` binary.

**Please focus on:**
- The `proutf` rewrite: in-place `strchr`/`*nl = '\0'` on its own buffer, and whether any caller depended on the all-in-one behaviour.
- Whether gating `battle.c:642` is the right call versus deleting it, and whether removing output from a Release build is properly justified as a fix rather than a regression (AGENTS.md requires deliberate plain-mode changes to be stated and explained; the commit will do so).
- Whether I have missed any other ungated diagnostic of the same family.
- The two test additions, including a **known weakness I want your judgement on**: the `journey.sh` `DEBUG:` check is opportunistic, because that journey plays a random galaxy and whether a base placement retries is chance — it caught the regression in 5 of 6 runs against a `main` binary. The combat check cannot bite at all until a seeded combat journey exists (issue #12, which is next). Both are commented as such. Is that acceptable, or should this branch carry a deterministic pin?

Explicit approve / request-changes verdict, please.

If you need a pty: tmux on your own socket via `-L <unique>` **and** `-f /dev/null`; never the default socket, never a bare `kill-server`, never `kill-session` on a session you did not create. Never redirect the game's stdout in a tmux session. Remove any `*.trk` you leave in the repo root.

## Verdict: **Approve** (two nits, neither blocking)

Reviewed state: branch `fix/tui-briefing-paging` at `19315ca` (no commits ahead of `main`) plus the five modified working-tree files — `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/sst.c`, `setup.c`, `battle.c`, `tests/journey.sh`, `tests/tui.sh`. No staged or untracked files. Nothing accidental in the tree; no `*.trk`, no debug leftovers, no unrelated edits.

### On the three things you asked about

**1. The `proutf` rewrite (`sst.c:781-803`) — correct.**
`buf` is an automatic array that `vsnprintf` always NUL-terminates, so `strchr`/`*nl = '\0'` on it is well defined, `p = nl + 1` can at worst land on the terminator, and the final `if (*p != '\0')` covers it. Truncation and the empty-result case degrade exactly as before.

No caller depends on the all-in-one behaviour. The only new observable is that `skip()` now runs between pieces, and `skip()`'s side effects are `linecount` and `pause(0)`, which touches only `proutn`/`prout`/`getch` — no path back into `proutf`. Two callers pass a leading `\n` (`reports.c:45`, `finish.c:78`), which now emits `proutn("")` first; harmless for both `fputs` and `waddstr`.

I verified plain mode independently rather than by argument: I built a baseline from `HEAD` carrying **only** the `setup.c`/`battle.c` gating (old `proutf`), and ran seven seeded Release journeys (`tournament 1,2,5,7,11,13,17`, long/expert, with movement, phasers, torpedoes, score and quit — journeys that do page, `[CONTINUE?]` appears in them). All seven are **byte-identical** to the branch. The `proutf` change on its own moves nothing for a plain-mode player.

**2. Gating `battle.c:642` rather than deleting it — right call, and the Release change is a fix.**
Gating matches the file's own idiom (`battle.c:555` `if (idebug) prout("ATTACK!")`, `battle.c:1443`), and the diagnostic still has value from a `debug` game. The `#ifdef DEBUG` wrapper is mandatory, not stylistic: `idebug` only exists under `DEBUG` (`sst.h:119`, `sst.h:218`).

Removing it from Release is a defect fix: it is a raw dump of two internal doubles that duplicates the player-facing `NN.NN unit hit on the Enterprise` printed a few lines above (`battle.c:626-636`), it appears nowhere in `sst.doc`, and no test asserted it. Per AGENTS.md the commit must state the plain-mode change — say specifically that the *only* Release plain-mode delta is that line's disappearance, and that the `proutf` rewrite contributes none.

I also checked the other direction, which the gating could plausibly have broken: with the `debug` password, `tournament 3` prints 6 `DEBUG:` lines on both the branch Debug build and a pristine baseline Debug build. The gate does not over-reach.

**3. Other ungated diagnostics of the same family — none left.**
I walked every `#ifdef DEBUG` region in all `.c` files and checked the enclosing condition of each print. Everything remaining is either inside an `if (idebug)` block (`ai.c:156/175/194/244`, `events.c:642`, `moving.c:590`, `setup.c:331`, `sst.c:406/416`) or inside `debugme()`/the interactive debug commands (`sst.c:835+`), which the player only reaches by asking. Outside `#ifdef DEBUG`, `battle.c:642` was the only one of this shape; `battle.c:1120`/`1192` (`"Energy available= "`) is a genuine phaser prompt. `main.c`'s `printf("Hello, World!\n")` is not in the CMake target, so it ships nothing.

### Findings

**Nit — `tests/tui.sh:336`**, `want "the rest of the briefing never arrived" "Good Luck!"` can fail on a galaxy the code got right. It asserts after `to_command`, so it depends on nothing else filling the ten-line window. Measured across 40 seeded starts, exactly 4 lines separate `Good Luck!` from `COMMAND>` — about six lines of headroom — but the starting quadrant is fully random (`setup.c:234 iran8(&quadx, &quady)`), and `newqad()` prints a 6-line Romulan-Neutral-Zone hail (`setup.c:672-681`) or a 3-line Thing hail (`setup.c:688-693`) when it qualifies. The RNZ case eats the headroom and can add a page pause on top. It did not occur in 40 samples, so this is rare, not likely. Fix, if you want it airtight: record the sighting *during* the loop rather than after it — poll for `Good Luck!` on each iteration of a `to_command`-shaped loop and set a flag, which also matches the comment's stated intent ("reachable", not "still on screen").

**Nit — `tests/journey.sh:178`**, `Hit [0-9.]+ energy` does not cover `%g`'s exponent form, so a hypothetical `Hit 1.2e-05 energy ...` would slip through. `Hit [0-9][^ ]* energy` costs nothing.

### On the opportunistic-check question

Acceptable to ship, but the "needs #12" framing is stronger than the facts for the **setup** half. The galaxy is already seedable without any new journey: `tournament <n>` calls `srand(n)` (`setup.c:447`). On a pristine Debug baseline, `tournament 3` prints exactly 6 `DEBUG:` lines, 3 runs out of 3; unseeded, I measured the chatter in 9 of 12 runs, matching your 10-of-12. So a deterministic pin for the `DEBUG:` half costs one changed answer in the script plus one extra `n` for the tournament-only "Do you want your score recorded?" prompt (`sst.c:492`).

The **combat** half genuinely does need #12 — a scripted fight needs game time, and the journey's own header explains why time-passing commands desynchronise a piped script.

My call: either ship as-is (the gate is a one-line change, the check never false-fails, and the comments are honest about it), or spend the five minutes on a seeded setup-only case. I would not hold the branch for it. If you do add a seeded case, consider pinning the positive direction too (`debug` password → the lines *do* print) — that is what stops a future tidy-up from deleting the diagnostics outright, and it is fully deterministic today.

### Not reviewed

- I took the verifier's linked-harness byte-equivalence and recursion results as given, per your instruction — though the seeded-journey comparison above re-establishes the plain-mode half independently.
- I did not run `tests/tui.sh` or drive a pty myself, so the 20/20 result and the 80x24 / 72x24 rendering are the verifier's; I reviewed the script by reading it.

Hygiene note: `git worktree list` still registers two leftovers from your earlier review attempts (`.../scratchpad/v3/base` and `.../scratchpad/wt`). `git worktree prune` before committing.

cd /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek
python3 - <<'PYEOF'
p='tests/tui.sh'
s=open(p).read()
def sub(a,b):
    global s
    assert s.count(a)==1, "count=%d %r" % (s.count(a), a[:60])
    s=s.replace(a,b)

sub('''want() {
	screen | grep -qF "$2" || { fail "$1"; dump; }
}''','''want() {
	screen | grep -qF "$2" || { fail "$1"; dump; }
}

# Like to_command, but reports in $saw whether $1 was on screen at any
# point along the way. For text meant to arrive and then scroll on:
# looking only once the prompt is back asks whether it is *still*
# there, which depends on how much the game had to say afterwards.
saw=""
to_command_seeing() {
	saw=""
	i=0
	while [ "$i" -lt 40 ]; do
		screen | grep -qF "$1" && saw=yes
		screen | grep -qF 'COMMAND' && return 0
		if screen | grep -qE 'CONTINUE|HIT SPACE BAR'; then
			tm send-keys -t "$pane" Space
		fi
		i=$((i + 1))
		sleep 0.25
	done
	return 1
}''')

sub('''if ! to_command; then
	fail "the game never reached its command prompt"
	dump
	exit 1
fi
# The rest of it survived the pause: the second half is reachable, not
# just the first half held.
want "the rest of the briefing never arrived" "Good Luck!"''',
'''if ! to_command_seeing 'Good Luck!'; then
	fail "the game never reached its command prompt"
	dump
	exit 1
fi
# The rest of it arrived after the pause: the second half is reachable,
# not just the first half held.
[ -n "$saw" ] || fail "the rest of the briefing never arrived"''')

**#25 is done** — [PR #29](https://github.com/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/pull/29), commit `ea703f2`, signed, all four CI legs green. Awaiting your merge before I start #12.

The fix itself is three lines of logic: `proutf()` prints its buffer a line at a time instead of handing the whole blob to `proutn()`, so the newlines inside it count toward paging. The briefing now stops after the mission and deadline, and the rest arrives on the next screen.

**What it exposed is the more interesting half.** Once newlines cost something, four developer diagnostics stopped being free — including `battle.c:642`, `Hit %g energy %g`, a raw dump of two internal doubles that duplicates the hit message printed three lines above it. It was printing **in every build including Release, on every enemy hit**, and it wasn't even inside `#ifdef DEBUG`. All four now sit behind the `debug` password.

I found that because the verifier **failed the branch**. I had claimed Release plain mode was byte-identical; it ran 320 seeded journeys, found 8 counterexamples, and — rather than just reporting them — deleted `battle.c:642` from both binaries, rebuilt, and reran to prove it was the sole cause. My claim was wrong and the commit message now says precisely what changes: that one line disappears from Release, nothing else moves, and neither build gains or loses a pause.

Two other things worth surfacing:

- The `journey.sh` `DEBUG:` check is **opportunistic**, and the PR says so. That journey plays a random galaxy, so whether a base placement retries is chance — it caught the regression in 5 of 6 runs. The combat check can't bite at all until a seeded combat journey exists. Both are commented in the file rather than left to look like coverage they aren't.
- Code review found my `Good Luck!` assertion could fail on a galaxy the code got *right* — a Romulan hail in the starting quadrant would scroll it off before the check ran. It now watches during the paging loop rather than sampling after it.

**On #12, which you asked for next:** it's the natural follow-on, and this PR just made the case for it twice over — a seeded combat journey is exactly what turns both of those weak checks into real ones. Say the word on merging #29 and I'll start.

--
## Goal

Extend automated coverage to the parts of the game the current journey test deliberately cannot reach: movement, combat, docking, and the events that fire as game time passes.

## Why the current test stops short

`tests/journey.sh` uses only commands that pass **no** game time. Anything that advances the clock can schedule an event, and an event's `[HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]` prompt calls `getch()` — which eats a byte of the piped script and desynchronises every command after it. That would make the test intermittently fail in a way that is very hard to diagnose, so movement was left out on purpose (the constraint is documented in the script's header comment).

## Suggested approach

Start a **tournament** game with a fixed number instead of `regular`. `setup.c` seeds with `srand((unsigned int)(int)aaitem)` from the tournament number, which makes the galaxy layout and every subsequent event roll reproducible. With a known seed you can script a journey that moves, fights, docks, and takes damage, and assert on specific outcomes.

Known caveat to design around: `rand()` differs between glibc and macOS libc, so a seeded journey is deterministic **per platform**, not across them. Options include per-platform expectation sets, asserting only on properties that hold under any seed, or shipping a small portable RNG for tests. Whatever the choice, a failure should be a hard, reproducible failure rather than a flake.

Also worth covering once movement works: paging behaviour (`[HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]`) with input that supplies the keypress.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test exercises movement, combat, and docking end to end.
- [ ] It is deterministic — run it at least 20 times in both Debug and Release with zero flakes.
- [ ] It passes on both Linux and macOS in CI, or is explicitly and visibly scoped to one platform.
- [ ] It stays bounded in time and output, like the existing journey (byte ceiling, timeout, CTest `TIMEOUT`).
- [ ] Registered with CTest so `ctest --test-dir build` runs it.

## Notes

`tests/journey.sh` is the model to follow — in particular the output ceiling, the exit-status capture inside the subshell, and the falsification habit of deleting a step to confirm the matching assertion actually fails.

Follow the workflow in [AGENTS.md](../blob/main/AGENTS.md).
